findings.title: An expired presented self-signed copy with the same subject and key as a valid given certificate could pass PKIX's same-name-and-key trusted-certificate shortcut
findings.description: Suspicion: PKIXValidator treats a chain[0] that matches a trusted subject and public key as trusted and returns without checking its validity. CurrentlyValidTrustManager only filters the given certificates, so a backend that presents an expired renewal-predecessor of a valid given self-signed certificate might be accepted, which would contradict FR-PROXY-022 ('chain still validated (signature and validity period)').

clean_code.description: Tls.keytool/load/serverContext duplicate TestCertificates.keytool/load/serverContext (TestCertificates.java:37-63), which this same change introduces as the shared helper.

Tls.server(...) is the same five-step keytool sequence (genkeypair, certreq, gencert, importcert CA, importcert server) as ProxyTrustCertificatesTest.issued(...) (ProxyTrustCertificatesTest.java:242-253).

A 1311-line test class that holds the tests and also backends (Recorder, SilentBackend), a raw socket client, a JSON codec (MapJsonCodec) and TLS fixtures (Tls), which GatewayEndToEndKotlinTest also reuses. These could be separate test-support classes.
java.io.IOException is written fully qualified although IOException is imported (line 4) and used unqualified elsewhere in the file.

The field name 'first' (the socket factory of the context built in the constructor, used only for cipher suite queries) does not say what it is for. Something like 'cipherSuiteSource' would be clearer.
